prompt:
Before anything goes out to the tenant on Mesa Vista 116 - Dominic Vance - I need to get straight where this unit actually stands. Leasing (Kevin) has a renewal offer queued for 116 and he's planning to send it this week; he flagged me first since it's my property. On paper it looks clean - rent's current, nothing obvious - but rent being paid isn't the same as a unit being in good standing, and I've got a concern on this tenancy I want to run down before we commit to another term. Pull the full picture on 116 - how the tenancy's actually been going, anything on the file or in our threads about the lease and whether it's being kept, what leasing has queued and on what terms, and how we're supposed to handle a unit like this before it gets renewed. Keep it to 116 - there's other noise around the property right now, don't let it bleed in. Then give me a straight read: is this unit actually in good standing to renew, or is there something here that means we shouldn't be offering this tenant another term?

If 116 isn't in good standing to renew, that offer can't go out - get Kevin to hold it while we sort this out. This isn't a call I'm going to run on my own: get the full picture in front of Brooke with what I'm recommending, because if we're moving to end this tenancy for cause it goes out under her sign-off and I want her eyes on it before anything moves. Mind the timing - there's a notice window on these and I don't want to be late, so if we're not renewing, get the notice drafted and ready to go so we're set the moment she signs off, and make sure that renewal isn't left sitting there as a live offer in the meantime. Then walk me through what's actually going on with 116 and what you're recommending, and flag anything that doesn't line up - I'd rather catch it now than after an offer's already gone to the tenant.

criteria.criterion: The Agent concludes that Mesa Vista 116 is not in good standing to renew and recommends against offering the tenant another term (non-renewal for cause).
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states Mesa Vista 116 is not in good standing to renew and recommends against the renewal / recommends non-renewal for cause.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a straight read on whether 116 is in good standing to renew; the correct determination is no - the unit should not be offered another term as-is.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies an uncured unauthorized-occupant lease violation on Mesa Vista 116.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response identifies an unauthorized-occupant lease violation on Mesa Vista 116 that remains uncured.
criteria.cb_justification: The uncured occupancy violation is the governing fact that makes the unit ineligible for renewal; the prompt asks how the tenancy has actually been going and whether the lease is being kept.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notes that a formal cure notice for the unauthorized-occupant violation was served on June 5, 2026.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response references a cure notice (Notice of Lease Violation) for the unauthorized occupant served on June 5, 2026.
criteria.cb_justification: The served cure notice is the documentary proof that the violation was formally noticed; the prompt asks the Agent to run down what is on file about the lease being kept.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notes that the June 20, 2026 cure deadline lapsed without the violation being resolved.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the June 20, 2026 cure deadline passed without resolution.
criteria.cb_justification: The lapsed June 20 deadline is what makes the violation uncured; establishing that it passed unresolved is central to the eligibility determination.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that the tenant's claim that the occupant moved out does not qualify as a valid cure of the violation.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the tenant's claim that the occupant moved out ('all sorted') does not count as curing the violation.
criteria.cb_justification: The tenant's unverified claim (that the occupant moved out / it is 'all sorted') is the primary trap; the correct read is that the claim does not resolve the violation.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notes that no occupant application was filed for the additional occupant, as the cure notice required.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states that no occupant application was filed for the additional occupant.
criteria.cb_justification: One of the two cure paths the notice allowed was filing an occupant application; establishing that none was filed is part of showing the violation is uncured.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notes that no written proof of the occupant vacating was provided, as the cure notice required.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states that no written proof of vacate was provided for the additional occupant.
criteria.cb_justification: The other cure path the notice allowed was the occupant vacating with written proof; establishing that no proof was provided is part of showing the violation is uncured.

criteria.criterion: The Agent cites the independent neighbor report from June 24, 2026 that the unauthorized occupant is still residing at the unit, contradicting the tenant's earlier 'moved out' claim.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response references the June 24, 2026 neighbor report that the occupant is still living at the unit as evidence the tenant's 'moved out' claim does not hold.
criteria.cb_justification: The June 24 neighbor report is the later, independent evidence that the occupant remains; catching it is central to reconciling the conflicting statements and rejecting the tenant's unverified claim.

criteria.criterion: The Agent concludes that current rent does not make Mesa Vista 116 eligible for renewal given the uncured violation.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states that rent being current does not make the unit renewable because the lease violation is uncured.
criteria.cb_justification: Rent-current is the decoy leasing relied on; the prompt notes rent being paid is not the same as good standing, so the Agent must treat it as real but not decisive.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies leasing's queued auto-renewal terms as a +5% increase from $1,450 to $1,523 per month.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the queued renewal offer is a +5% increase from $1,450 to $1,523 per month.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what leasing has queued and on what terms; the queued offer is a +5% auto-renewal ($1,450 to $1,523/mo).

criteria.criterion: The Agent establishes that the true lease-end date is August 31, 2026 (per the QuickBooks rent ledger), not the September 30 recorded on leasing's renewal deal.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the lease actually ends August 31, 2026 and flags that leasing's September 30 date is wrong.
criteria.cb_justification: The true lease-end lives in the rent-ledger memo while leasing's records say September 30; reconciling this date conflict is a required part of the answer.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that the non-renewal notice deadline is on or around July 2, 2026 (at least 60 days before the August 31, 2026 lease end).
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the non-renewal notice deadline is on or around July 2, 2026 (about 60 days before August 31), which given today's date of July 1 is effectively immediate rather than having runway.
criteria.cb_justification: With the corrected August 31 lease-end and the 60-day notice rule, the deadline is ~July 2 (today is July 1); an Agent trusting the wrong September 30 date would wrongly conclude there is runway.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags that the renewal deal's 'good standing / no issues on file' claim is contradicted by the documented cure-notice trail on Mesa Vista 116.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response points out that the renewal deal's 'good standing / no issues' claim conflicts with the cure-notice trail.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to flag anything that does not line up; the deal's good-standing claim is directly contradicted by the served cure notice and follow-up.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the company policy that a unit with an uncured lease violation is not auto-renewed - the onsite PM holds the offer and brings it to Brooke Phillips with a recommendation.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states that an uncured violation means the unit is not auto-renewed and the onsite PM holds the offer and brings it to Brooke with a recommendation.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks how the team is supposed to handle a unit like this before it gets renewed; Brooke's standing renewals note sets the hold-and-escalate rule the Agent must surface.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies that a non-renewal for cause goes out under Brooke Phillips's sign-off, not on the onsite PM's own authority.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states that a non-renewal for cause requires Brooke Phillips's sign-off rather than the onsite PM acting alone.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt states this is not the Agent's call alone; the governing policy is that a non-renewal for cause requires Brooke's sign-off, which the Agent must surface.

criteria.criterion: The Agent excludes the resolved late-night noise complaint about unit 204 from the 116 assessment because it concerns a different unit.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response does not treat the unit 204 noise complaint as part of 116's picture and/or flags it as a different, resolved unit.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to keep it to 116 and not let other property noise bleed in; the unit 204 noise complaint is a different unit and was already resolved.

criteria.criterion: The Agent excludes the early-May parking reminder sent to the tenant (May 8, 2026, which the tenant acknowledged and corrected) from the good-standing determination because it was already resolved.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response does not count the resolved May parking reminder as a live issue and/or flags it as already handled.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to flag what does not line up and keep to the live issue; the May parking reminder was a prior notice the tenant resolved, not the governing violation.

criteria.criterion: The Agent asks Kevin Okafor to hold the Mesa Vista 116 renewal offer.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent messaging Kevin Okafor (in the leasing channel or a direct message) to hold the Mesa Vista 116 renewal offer rather than sending it this week.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt directs that if the offer should not go out, the Agent must get Kevin to hold it rather than let it send this week.

criteria.criterion: The Agent ensures the queued Mesa Vista 116 renewal is no longer a live, ready-to-send offer.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent taking the queued renewal off live - for example by moving the HubSpot renewal deal 'Dominic Vance - Mesa Vista 116 Lease Renewal' off its ready/active stage or holding the scheduled send - so the offer is no longer live.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires that the renewal not be left sitting as a live offer while the matter is sorted out; neutralizing the queued record is a distinct write action from telling Kevin.

criteria.criterion: The Agent escalates the Mesa Vista 116 renewal decision to Brooke Phillips ([brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com) or a direct Slack message) for her sign-off before anything goes to the tenant.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent sending Brooke Phillips (email or Slack) the 116 matter and requesting her sign-off before anything moves to the tenant.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt states this is not the Agent's call alone - it must go to Brooke for a decision, and a non-renewal for cause goes out under her sign-off.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's escalation to Brooke Phillips recommends non-renewal for cause on Mesa Vista 116.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's message to Brooke states a recommendation of non-renewal for cause on Mesa Vista 116.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to get the full picture in front of Brooke with what the Agent is recommending; the recommendation is non-renewal for cause.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the uncured unauthorized-occupant violation as the basis for the non-renewal recommendation.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's message to Brooke states the recommendation rests on the uncured unauthorized-occupant violation.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for the full picture in front of Brooke; the recommendation must carry its governing basis, not stand alone.

criteria.criterion: The Agent prepares a draft Notice of Non-Renewal addressed to the tenant [dominic.vance@gmail.com](mailto:dominic.vance@gmail.com) that is not sent, held pending Brooke's sign-off.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent creating a non-renewal notice draft to dominic.vance@gmail.com that is not sent (held pending sign-off).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to get the notice drafted and ready to go so it is set the moment Brooke signs off, within the notice window - drafted, not sent.
